| **Assessed** | 2026-11-27 |

The value of human labour nears zero in many sectors and growth shifts to capital, risking a narrow elite owning the productive economy while most people are shut out. A universal basic capital stake and an income floor keep people sharing in AI-driven growth.

## Social contract scores (draft)

| Promise | Score | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hard work pays | 1 | Labour's marginal product approaches zero in many sectors and the public is locked out of a meaningful role in the productive economy; UBC's stake regardless of work status replaces rather than keeps the promise. |
| Affordable essentials |  | Not addressed: the extract says nothing on the cost of housing, food, energy or care. |
| Reliable safety net | 3 | The NIT becomes a universal income floor and UBC adds a capital underpinning so citizens are protected immediately, though levels and funding are unstated. |
| Responsive government |  | Not addressed: UBC's panel Democratic Voice score rates the policy; the extract does not describe government in the scenario. |
| Time for what matters |  | Not addressed: the extract says nothing on working time, family or community in this scenario. |

## Policies from the atlas

- **Universal Basic Capital / Equity** (`universal-basic-capital`): A pre-designed Universal Basic Capital is paired with the income floor so citizens retain a durable ownership stake in capital-driven growth.
- **Tax Credit Expansion** (`tax-credit-expansion`): The Scenario 2 NIT "could soon after function as a universal income floor as earned wages declined".
- **Unemployment Benefits** (`unemployment-benefits`): By this stage, the Scenario 1 stabilizers (expanded UI and EITC) and the Scenario 2 NIT are in place.
